question.text: The maximum frequency for reflection of sky waves from a certain layer of the ionosphere is found to be <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><msub><mi mathvariant="normal">f</mi><mi>max</mi></msub><mo> </mo><mo>=</mo><mo> </mo><mn>9</mn><mo> </mo><mo>(</mo><msub><mi mathvariant="normal">N</mi><mi>max</mi></msub><msup><mo>)</mo><mrow><mn>1</mn><mo>/</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow></msup></math>, where <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><msub><mi mathvariant="normal">N</mi><mi>max</mi></msub></math> is the maximum electron density at that layer of the ionosphere. On a certain day, it is observed that signals of frequencies higher than <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>8</mn><mo> </mo><mi>MHz</mi></math> are not received by reflection from the <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><msub><mi mathvariant="normal">F</mi><mn>2</mn></msub></math> layer of the ionosphere. Estimate the maximum electron densities of the <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><msub><mi mathvariant="normal">F</mi><mn>2</mn></msub></math> layers on that day.

solution.text:
The maximum frequency for reflection of sky waves

fmax = 9(Nmax)1/2

where Nmax is a maximum electron density.

For F2 layer,

 fmax=8 MHz

So, 8×106=9(Nmax)1/2

maximum electron density,Nmax=8×10692=7·9×1011 m-3
